inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: Instruction says to keep going until every row is complete, with retries and sub agent spawning, but runtime notes declare no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents.

elements.name: Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Hard spend cap or per-run quota on enrichment API use
Max unattended steps, retries, and sub-agent depth
Spend and quota exhaustion alerting on enrichment account

findings.title: Spend loop (TC6): unbounded retries and recursive delegation can exhaust the shared enrichment quota

evidence.observation: The prompt directs the agent to retry failed lookups, spawn researcher sub agents, and keep going until every row is complete.
There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers.
enrich.lookup is billed per call and the API key and monthly quota are shared with sales and marketing, so exhaustion affects other teams.
The nightly batch is 40,000 rows and about 3 percent of rows have malformed company names that never return a complete result, creating a persistent retry population.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account.

recommendations.action: Enforce a per-run and monthly spend cap for enrich.lookup, with fail-closed behavior when the cap is reached.
Set hard limits on retries, unattended steps, and recursive sub-agent spawning depth; terminate rows that exceed the limit and route them to a review queue.
Add spend and quota exhaustion alerts with ownership and response thresholds before shared quota depletion impacts other teams.

forecast.watch_signal: Median steps or runtime per batch rises, retry counts increase, or the product goal expands beyond basic enrichment without adding hard runtime and spend limits.

stride_coverage.rationale: No inbound protocol peer, external authentication surface, or identity claim for this standalone batch agent is described in the provided artifacts.
The artifacts do not show self-configuration or mutable tool definitions; the assessed risk here is runaway operation, not config tampering.
No human approval or disputed user-attributed action path is described; this batch process acts under a shared service account by design.
The design does not expose an egress path carrying CRM data outside the trust boundary; the paid API capability is scored for spend impact, not disclosure.
No evidence shows the agent can obtain or exercise privileges beyond the shared enrichment and CRM service capabilities already declared.
The CRM batch source is internal and no identity verification or impersonation scenario is described in the provided design artifacts.
This source is a scheduled internal batch feed, not a human-originated request where origin disputes or non-repudiation controls are material.
The batch input flow does not cross a trust boundary, so STRIDE flow coverage does not require tampering assessment for this internal-only path.
The batch input flow remains inside the trust domain and no external transport or boundary crossing is described for these CRM rows.
This internal flow itself is not the source of the denial condition; the missing spend and step limits on downstream actions create the finding instead.
The artifacts do not say whether outbound enrichment API traffic has integrity controls, pinned endpoints, or request mutation protections.
The artifacts do not specify transport encryption, payload logging, or exact fields sent to the enrichment API across the trust boundary.
The artifacts identify a shared API key and quota store, but do not describe protections against unauthorized modification or key rotation controls.
The artifacts do not say where the shared API key is stored or whether access to the key and quota state is restricted and monitored.

rating.rationale: Present risk is driven by a property failure rather than an external attack path: the design has unbounded retries, runtime, and recursive delegation on a billed shared quota. Under rubric section 5a, the affected capabilities include spend and delegate, so the property finding is consequential. No declared or verified structural controls restore the missing spend cap, step limit, or quota alerting properties, so residual remains at the inherent floor. Forecast does not rise above present because the design is already fully exposed without needing an additional trigger.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior or production telemetry.

No runtime configuration, orchestration policy, billing guardrail configuration, or monitoring configuration was provided, so the absence of spend caps, step limits, and alerts is assessed from the supplied notes only.
No source code or sub-agent implementation details were provided, so the exact recursion mechanics and failure-handling logic are not independently verified.
